content: Root cause: The bug was caused by the condition in the while loop that checks the value of `read`. The original condition `if (read < 0)` only handled the case when the end of the stream was reached, but it did not account for the scenario where `read` could be zero, which indicates that no bytes were read from the stream. This could lead to an infinite loop if the stream is not producing any more data but is not yet closed. The patch modifies the condition to `if (read <= 0)`, which correctly handles both the end of the stream and the case where no bytes are read, thus preventing the test from timing out.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by the condition in the while loop that checks the value of `read`. The original condition `if (read < 0)` only handled the case when the end of the stream was reached, but it did not account for the scenario where `read` could be zero, which indicates that no bytes were read from the stream. This could lead to an infinite loop if the stream is not producing any more data but is not yet closed. The patch modifies the condition to `if (read <= 0)`, which correctly handles both the end of the stream and the case where no bytes are read, thus preventing the test from timing out.

@@ -444,7 +444,7 @@ public void testReadFileContent() throws Exception {
       int read; 
       while (true) {
         read = fsdis.read(buffer, readIntoBuffer, buffer.length - readIntoBuffer);
-        if (read < 0) {
+        if (read <= 0) {
           // end of stream:
